predict.question: If you dip turmeric paper into lemon juice and into soapy water, what will happen?

options.text: Turmeric stays yellow in both, since both are just kitchen liquids
Turmeric stays yellow in lemon juice but turns reddish-brown in soapy water
Lemon juice is always dangerous so it will burn the paper, while soap is harmless and does nothing

predict.why: Turmeric indicator turns reddish-brown in basic (soapy) solutions but stays yellow in acidic or neutral ones, showing a real chemical difference, not just taste or danger.

experiment.title: Turmeric Indicator Test
steps: Rub a little turmeric powder mixed with water on strips of paper and let them dry (or ask adult to help dry faster)
Make a soapy water solution in a bowl
Squeeze lemon juice into another bowl with a little water
Dip one turmeric paper strip into the lemon water and note the colour
Dip another turmeric paper strip into the soapy water and note the colour
Compare both strips side by side
experiment.note: Keep hands away from eyes while handling turmeric and soap; wash hands after the activity.

say: What colour do you see on each strip?
Why do you think lemon and soap gave different colours?
Does sour taste always mean the same thing as this colour change?
avoid: Don't say 'lemon is acid and soap is base' before they notice the colours themselves

notice.question: What did you see on the two turmeric strips?
notice.lookFor: Child notices the strip in soapy water turned reddish-brown while the one in lemon stayed yellow, and connects this to a real difference between the liquids.

hints.text: Look closely at the colour of each paper strip, not just the liquid.
Compare the strip from lemon juice with the strip from soapy water - are they the same?
One liquid changed the turmeric colour and the other didn't - this tells you something about what's inside each liquid.

reveal.explanation: Substances can be acidic, basic or neutral, and this is a chemical property, not about taste or danger. Lemon juice is acidic and keeps turmeric yellow. Soapy water is basic and turns turmeric reddish-brown. An indicator like turmeric changes colour differently with acids and bases, letting us test substances without tasting them.
reveal.termMeaning: A substance that changes colour to show whether something is acidic or basic.

teachBack.prompt: Explain to a younger sibling why turmeric paper is used to test if something is acidic or basic, using what you saw with lemon and soap.

revisits.question: If you dip turmeric paper in baking soda water, what colour do you expect?
revisits.answer: Reddish-brown, because baking soda solution is basic like soap.

revisits.question: Would vinegar turn turmeric paper reddish-brown or keep it yellow?
revisits.answer: It stays yellow because vinegar is acidic, like lemon juice.
